option_relations.rationale: The clinical presentation and diagnostic findings, including the presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and the brain biopsy results, are consistent with Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma (PCNSL).
Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma is a distinct clinical entity that does not match the presentation and diagnostic findings in this case.
Secondary CNS involvement by systemic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma would typically involve a known history of systemic lymphoma, which is not present in this case.
Lymphomatosis cerebri variant of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a subtype of PCNSL, but the specific diagnosis in this case is more consistent with PCNSL.
